The test image shows a corn leaf with elongated, cigar/canoe-shaped tan lesions. This is a **leaf** disease. Top candidates: Northern_Leaf_Blight, Goss_S_Wilt, Gray_Leaf_Spot, Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight, Stewart_S_Disease, Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback, Carbonum_Leaf_Spot, Eyespot.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with my top candidate.
NLB reference shows very similar cigar-shaped tan lesions. Strong match. Now let me check other candidates.
Goss's Wilt looks very different - large water-soaked areas with wavy edges and dark freckles. Not a match.
Gray Leaf Spot shows narrow rectangular lesions bounded by veins - very different from the test image's broader cigar-shaped lesions.
SCLB shows smaller, more rectangular lesions with reddish-brown margins - different from the test image.
Stewart's Disease shows long bleached streaks running the length of the leaf - different pattern from the test image's discrete cigar-shaped lesions.
Anthracnose shows smaller lesions with dark brown/purple margins along leaf edges - different from the test image.
Carbonum Leaf Spot shows many small circular spots - very different from the test image. Now let me view one more candidate (Eyespot) to complete 8 classes.

Eyespot shows many small circular spots with halos - completely different from the test image.

All 8 reference views used. The test image clearly matches Northern Leaf Blight: the lesions are elongated, cigar/canoe-shaped, tan to gray, several inches long, which is the hallmark of NLB. No other candidate came close visually.
